**How the proof works:** to show `x ∙ y ≈ y ∙ x`, I used the hypothesis `sq` with the arguments swapped (`sq y x`) inside a chain of rewrites:

`y ∙ ((x ∙ y) ∙ x) ≈ y ∙ (x ∙ (y ∙ x)) ≈ (y ∙ x) ∙ (y ∙ x) ≈ (y ∙ y) ∙ (x ∙ x) ≈ y ∙ (y ∙ (x ∙ x)) ≈ y ∙ ((y ∙ x) ∙ x)`

Each step is either associativity or `sq y x`. Cancelling `y` on the left (`∙-cancelˡ`) and then `x` on the right (`∙-cancelʳ`) leaves exactly `x ∙ y ≈ y ∙ x`.
